title: Portfolio-match hiring & credit-allowance scenario scan
body:
Executive summary:
This sheet evaluates three levers together: (1) portfolio-level headcount allocation across Hosted API / Dedicated / Private product lines, (2) the proposal to introduce a tiered credit-allowance (free credits + rollover) for new PLG users, and (3) pricing sensitivity scenarios for token/unit price movements. The intent is to produce a compact runbook that maps pricing shocks to hiring/credit-burn actions and to quantify near-term runway and unit economics tradeoffs.

Key conclusions (draft):
- Introducing a limited credit-allowance (30–60 USD new-user credit, 90 day expiry, 30% expected redemption) materially increases CAC-first-month burn but improves 90-day retention; net ARR uplift only when conversion delta > 3.5 p.p.
- Small pricing adjustments (-10% to +15% around baseline) generate asymmetric impacts on required FTE hiring across Hosted API vs Dedicated: Hosted is more elastic (higher volume response), Dedicated demand is more inelastic but has higher margin per request.
- Recommended short-term posture: freeze large hiring for product lines with <2.5x payback on incremental CAC under the -10% price scenario; pilot credit-allowance in US region only for 6–8 weeks and instrument conversion cohorts.

Assumptions and definitions:
- Baseline price: $0.012 per 1k tokens (hosted generation baseline, hypothetical for modeling).
- Token mix: 70% generation (avg 350 tokens/request), 30% embeddings/rerank (avg 10 tokens/unit).
- Hosted API average revenue per customer-month: $2,400 (baseline cohort).
- Dedicated average revenue per contract-month: $18,000 (baseline mid-market).
- Margins: baseline gross margin hosted = 48%, dedicated = 64% (after pooling infra and support costs).
- CAC baseline: Hosted = $450 (trial-heavy), Dedicated = $5,200 (sales-assisted).
- Credit-allowance proposal: 60 USD credit, expected redemption fraction 30%, incremental conversion uplift 4.0 p.p. over 90 days for cohorts exposed to credit.

Headcount plan snapshot (FTEs) - portfolio allocation (roll-forward quarters):
Header: Function, Q1-2027, Q2-2027, Q3-2027, Notes
Rows:
- Product (Hosted API), 8, 9, 9, "Feature & onboarding improvements prioritized if conversion lift low"
- Platform (Serving/infra), 14, 15, 16, "Scale reliability for Dedicated capacity"
- Sales (Dedicated), 6, 7, 8, "Ramp tied to committed capacity deals"
- Solutions/SE, 4, 5, 6, "Support Dedicated pre-sales"
- Finance & RevOps, 3, 3, 3, "Monitoring pricing experiments"
- Customer Success, 5, 6, 6, "Manage credit cohorts and churn"
Total FTEs by quarter: 40, 45, 48

Budget lines (simplified P&L impact of hires + credit program) - annualized view (USDk):
Header: Line, Baseline FY27, Incremental from hires, Credit program 6-12m, Notes
Rows:
- Personnel Opex, 10,200, 1,200, 0, "Incremental hires cost incl benefits"
- Infrastructure (GPU/Cloud), 6,000, 900, 60, "credit-driven short-run infra"
- Marketing & Trials, 1,400, 200, 180, "credit campaign spend + promo"
- Sales & AE comp, 2,800, 600, 0, "ramp for Dedicated"
- Total OpEx, 20,400, 2,900, 240, "rough order"

Pricing sensitivity scenarios (hosted generation primary):
Header: Scenario, Price delta, Elasticity (d% volume / d% price), Net impact on revenue, Impact on gross margin, Implication for hiring
Rows:
- Base, 0%, 0, 0, baseline margins, "No change"
- Soft (price -10%), -10%, +18% volume (assumed elastic), -3.2% revenue (net), gross margin down ~ -4 p.p., "Delay hosted hiring; free credit burn increases infra by ~3%"
- Promo (introduce credits), effective price equivalent -7% first 3 months due to redeemed credits, volume +25% for cohorts, CAC +$60 per converted customer, long-term payback depends on +4.0 p.p. conversion lift sustained
- Premium (+15%), +15%, -9% volume (assumed), +3.9% revenue (net), gross margin +2–3 p.p., "Invest in Dedicated sales and customer success; accelerate platform hires"

Token-level unit economics sensitivity (per 1k tokens):
Header: Price per 1k tokens, Volume sensitivity multiplier (relative), Gross margin, Net unit contribution
Rows:
- $0.010, x1.18, 44%, 0.0044
- $0.012 (base), x1.00, 48%, 0.00576
- $0.014, x0.92, 50%, 0.0070
- $0.018 (premium), x0.82, 52%, 0.00936
Notes: unit contribution approximated = price * margin. Volume multiplier derived from elasticity assumptions; small-packages (embeddings) less elastic.

Impact matrix (5 actionable triggers):
1) If -10% price scenario leads to >10% infra cost growth vs baseline and Hosted cohort payback > 6 months -> hiring freeze for Hosted product engineers; convert hiring budget to SRE/infra optimization.
2) If credit cohort conversion uplift <2.0 p.p. in pilot -> sunset credit program and reallocate $180k marketing to targeted product funnel improvements.
3) If Dedicated committed ARR pipeline >$4.0M (12m) -> accelerate SE hiring (2 FTEs) and pre-commit one capacity pool.
4) If gross margin dips >3 p.p. company-wide -> temporary capex on burst GPUs and pause broad promotions.
5) If unit contribution increases by >20% in premium scenario -> reprice enterprise tiers and accelerate cross-sell coverage.

Sensitivity tab (quick view) - discrete scenario outputs (annualized USDk):
Header: Scenario, ARR delta vs base, Incremental OpEx, Change in gross profit, Headcount change recommended
Rows:
- Price -10%, -1,800, +320, -920, "-4 FTEs (defer hires)"
- Credit pilot (US-only), +420, +240, +60, "+2 FTEs (CS & growth)"
- Price +15%, +2,160, +580, +1,180, "+6 FTEs (sales + platform)"

Experiment plan & instrumentation (high level):
- Week 0–4: implement credit pilot, US-only, cohort tagging, A/B: control vs credit; wire telemetry (signup, time-to-first-paid, 90-day churn).
- Week 5–8: analyze conversion lift, CAC delta, infra spike; stop/start credits if conversion uplift <2.0 p.p. or infra breaches +8% above forecast.
- Week 9–12: extend pilot to EU region only if cohort metrics positive; present readout to exec finance + product ops.

Open questions & risks (notes to reviewers):
- Elasticity assumptions are coarse; recommend adding 2nd-order model for usage intensity by customer segment (chat-heavy vs embedding-heavy).
- Conversion-to-revenue lag for credit cohorts could be longer than 90 days in some verticals; stress-test 6–9 month payback.
- Contractual discounts & enterprise negotiation flexibility complicates simple price move pass-through; model needs repo of active discount schedules.

Action items (owners):
- Build cohort instrumentation (Growth/Analytics) -> Noah Kim -> due 2026-12-16
- Run credit pilot configuration + legal T&C refresh -> Product Ops -> Emily Zhao -> due 2026-12-10
- Revised hire prioritization and freeze rules -> Finance -> Aisha Patel -> due 2026-12-05
- Dedicated sales pipeline cadence -> Sales leadership -> Marco Hernandez -> review 2026-12-08

Appendix: raw micro-scenarios and sensitivity inputs (abbreviated)
- Elasticity mapping: Hosted generation elasticity = -1.8 price elasticity; embeddings = -0.3.
- Cost per 1k tokens (infrastructure blended) = $0.0062 (baseline), with incremental infra per credit redemption = ~$0.0005 per redeemed token equivalent.
- Hire cost assumptions: avg fully-loaded = $150k/yr for engineers, $120k/yr for SE/CS, $210k/yr for senior AE.

Document history / notes:
- Drafted by Aisha Patel (Finance) with inputs from Marco H., Emily Z., Noah K.
- This is an operational working sheet intended for review by CFO + Product + GTM.
- Next formal version should include per-region modeling and a 24-month cash runway overlay.

End of sheet.
